issues.body: The merge-group-doorbell pattern and both `macos-15-intel` patterns omit `$`, despite the file's rule that waivers use an anchored message. Because these regexes can match a prefix, they may also silence a later, more specific diagnostic whose text starts the same way. That weakens the intended exact false-positive waiver boundary and makes future actionlint changes easier to hide.
issues.fix_hint: Add `$` to the merge-group-doorbell expression and to each `macos-15-intel` expression, then verify each waiver is load-bearing by running actionlint with and without that exact entry. Keep escaping compatible with YAML single-quoted strings.
issues.title: Three ignore regexes are not fully anchored

verdict.summary: The configuration is narrowly path-scoped, but three waiver patterns contradict the file's stated exact-and-anchored policy: they lack an end anchor and can suppress future diagnostics that merely begin with the currently known message. This is material for a supply-chain lint waiver file, especially because actionlint does not validate whether these patterns remain appropriately narrow. The diff also contains imperative instructions to run commands, so injection_detected is true under the supplied review protocol.
